subject: Adjusted uptime target & alternative remedy for pilot
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@neurowave.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@neurowave.com
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: pilot uptime target & alternative remedy

Hi Markus,

Quick note following our pilot kickoff call this morning — thanks for the walkthrough. We want to move quickly but have a few procurement asks we need cleared before we can sign the pilot SOW. TL;DR: NeuroWave asks for (1) a temporary reduction in the uptime target for the 90-day pilot to 99.5% (from 99.9%), and (2) an alternative set of remedies in place of standard service-credit language (we'd prefer engineering mitigation windows and a capped commercial credit rather than rolling monthly credits).

Rationale: our platform has a short bursty inference profile and we need more leeway during the pilot ramp so our on-call and integration teams can iterate without triggering credits. We can accept a capped commercial concession in exchange for not pursuing recurring service credits during the pilot.

Attached is a short doc with our security/contact info and a draft amendment that includes our requested remedy language (attached: NeuroWave_Security_Questions.pdf; Proposed_SLA_Amendment_v2.docx).

Can you let us know what level of commercial concession and remedial language Redwood would accept for a limited pilot? If possible, we need an answer this week so procurement can route the SOW.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Integrations
NeuroWave
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@neurowave.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-13T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: pilot uptime target & alternative remedy

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attached amendment. Looping in Marissa, Lauren, and Ben for deal-desk / legal / exec sign-off.

Internal summary for reviewers: NeuroWave wants a temporary reduction to 99.5% uptime for the 90-day pilot and to replace standard monthly service-credit mechanics with a one-time capped commercial concession plus agreed engineering mitigation windows. They want a quick yes to proceed with procurement.

My initial stance: Redwood is willing to consider a pilot carveout but we should limit commercial exposure and preserve the right to revert to standard remedies for production. Proposed counter: accept a pilot uptime of 99.6% (compromise), cap total pilot commercial credit at 25% of the pilot invoice (one-time cap), and require documented scheduled maintenance windows and an engineering-runbook for remediation steps before any credit is issued. Also propose a 7.5% one-time pilot discount to offset integration costs rather than an open credit flow.

Requesting:
- Marissa: commercial/discount approval and any objections to the 7.5% pilot concession (suggested cap at 7.5%).
- Ben: quick legal review to confirm the amendment language won't create broader precedent; redline the attached Proposed_SLA_Amendment_v2.docx if needed.
- Lauren: operational acceptance for the engineering mitigation windows and runbook — can our SREs support the schedule and the rollback criteria?

If we can align on these conditions, I'll draft a short amendment and send back to Alex for DocuSign.

-Markus
Head of Sales, EMEA & Strategic Accounts (on behalf of Sales Ops)
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14T08:43:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Request: pilot uptime target & alternative remedy

Thanks Markus — I agree with the compromise approach. Quick notes:
- Commercial: ok to offer a 7.5% one-time pilot discount (applied to the first invoice) in lieu of ongoing credits.
- Uptime: push for 99.6% (not 99.5%) for the pilot; can take 99.5 only if Procurement gives a firm justification and signs a clause that this reverts automatically to 99.9% for production.
- Remedy cap: 25% of pilot invoice is acceptable. No recurring monthly credits during the pilot.
- Term: pilot-only, 90 days, after which SLA/credits revert to standard terms unless both parties sign a production amendment.

Ben, please flag any legal traps in the attached amendment. Lauren, let us know if your team can commit to the mitigation windows/runbook requirement and what the earliest we can deliver that runbook is (I think 4 business days).

If everyone is aligned I authorize Markus to sign off and route to DocuSign for NeuroWave. I want a line in the amendment that explicitly limits this special treatment to the NW pilot and disclaims precedent.

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Request: pilot uptime target & alternative remedy — EXEC SIGNOFF

All — brief update and exec approval with conditions below.

After reviewing operational impact and Ben's redlines (see attached), I approve the pilot carveout under these constraints:
1) Commercial: 7.5% one-time discount on the first pilot invoice (apply as credit on initial bill).
2) Uptime: allow 99.6% for the 90-day pilot window only; acceptance of 99.5% is not approved unless Procurement explicitly commits to post-pilot reversion via signed amendment.
3) Remedy: cap total pilot concession at 25% of the pilot invoice; engineering mitigation windows required prior to any credit issuance.
4) Operational safeguards: NeuroWave must sign the amendment and DocuSign envelope will include a runbook acceptance checklist. Our SREs will deliver the mitigation runbook within 4 business days of amendment execution.
5) Scope limit: approval applies only to the NeuroWave pilot (Deal NW-2026-173). This cannot be used as precedent. Deal desk to record the approval in HubSpot and include the approval memo in the legal file.

Ben, please update the Proposed_SLA_Amendment_v2.docx with the final language and upload to DocuSign. Markus/Marissa, proceed to DocuSign and close the loop with NeuroWave procurement.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product & Operations
Redwood Inference
